chunks: Abu al-Hasan narrated to us, he said: Ali ibn Ahmad al-Tabari narrated to us, he said: Abu Sa'id narrated to us, he said: Karrash narrated to us, he said: Our master Anas narrated to us, he said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said:

Whoever recites one hundred verses will not be recorded among the heedless, and whoever recites two hundred verses will be recorded among the devoted, and whoever recites three hundred verses, the Quran will not argue with him. - Meaning: whoever memorizes that amount of the Quran, it is said: 'The boy has recited the Quran' when he has memorized it -.

key_terms.الْغَافِلِينَ: the heedless or those who neglect divine reminders
key_terms.لَمْ يُحَاجْهُ الْقُرْآنُ: the Quran will not argue with him (on Judgment Day)

ai.seo_question: What are the spiritual benefits of reciting 100, 200, and 300 verses of the Quran?
ai.summary: Recorded by Shaykh al-Saduq in *Ma'ani al-Akhbar*, this hadith emphasizes the transformative power of Quranic engagement, linking quantitative recitation to qualitative spiritual states. It illustrates the progression from escaping heedlessness (*ghafilin*) to attaining devotion (*qazin*) and finally achieving a state where the Quran becomes an ally rather than an adversary on the Day of Judgment. This reflects the Shia scholarly understanding that consistent engagement with the text shapes one's spiritual identity and eschatological standing.
